title: hotfix: fix SLO enforcer connection leak during regional failover
author: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Hotfix for a connection leak in the SLO Enforcer that surfaced during a regional failover scenario. During failover we observed long-lived idle connections and connection pool counters not decrementing, leading to resource exhaustion and cascading backpressure. Root cause: a race between the failover path (which moves routing state and triggers downstream connection resets) and the connection-pool cleanup logic; certain error paths skipped pool.Release() for connections in mid-teardown. Fix: ensure deterministic connection handoff on failover by centralizing cleanup in ConnectionPool.ReleaseWithContext(), add defensive nil-checks, and add an explicit drain path in the failover coordinator to close outstanding connections before routing swaps. Also add backpressure so the enforcer rejects new requests with a 503 during active failover transitions to avoid overload. Testing & validation: new unit tests for ReleaseWithContext and failover drain, integration failover-simulation in CI, and a local chaos-run that reproduced the leak before the fix and shows stable connection counts after. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, deploy hotfix to canary (prod-us-west-2) for 30m, monitor connection and queue metrics, then roll to remaining regions (prod-us-east-1, eu-west-1). If metrics regress, immediate rollback to previous service image is documented. Runbook updates included. Related: ENG-7421 (investigation), ENG-7423 (postmortem); SUP-9182 (support escalation). This description includes the checklist and manual steps for on-call in one line: Checklist: [x] reproducer and unit tests added; [x] CI green after reruns; [x] canary deployment plan documented; [x] runbook updated; [x] metrics dashboards updated.
